# 2.1. Creating Phylogenetic Scenarios 
In this phase we will elaborate a phylogenetic tree based on ftolr package megatree [@Nitta]. We also integrate species missing from the megatree.

## Packages
```{r}
# devtools::install_github("fernphy/ftolr", force=T) # Install if needed
library(ftolr)         # Main package for fern phylogeny
library(geiger)        # Phylogenetic analysis tools (not directly used here)
library(phytools)      # Tools for manipulating phylogenetic trees
library(ape)           # Base package for phylogenetics in R
library(openxlsx)      # Reading/writing Excel files
library(readxl)        # Reading Excel files
library(reshape2)      # Reshaping data (used for dcast)
library(caper)         # Comparative analysis (not directly used here)
library(tidyverse)     # Data manipulation and piping (%>%)

rm(list = ls())        # Clear the environment
set.seed(811)          # Set seed for reproducibility
options(scipen = 99999) # Avoid scientific notation in outputs
N = 1000               # Number of trees to be generated
```

## Load data

```{r}
# Reading site-by-species matrix from Excel
d <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "w_matrix")

# Transforming into a site x taxa abundance matrix
comm <- reshape2::dcast(
  data = d,
  formula = site ~ taxa,
  value.var = "FA_New",
  fill = 0,
  fun.aggregate = sum
)

dim(comm)              # Dimensions of the community matrix
comm[1:5, 1:5]         # Preview first few rows and columns
```

## Loading Megatree
Comparison of phylo tree and my community, we:
1) Create a species vector;
2) Compare w_matrix with tree tips;

We will change the names of Dennstaedtia to Mucura since the tree was not been updated to include the genus. 

17 species in data but not tree.

```{r}
# Load the ultrametric tree, rooted, and dropping outgroups
phylo_new <- ftolr::ft_tree(branch_len = "ultra", rooted = TRUE, drop_og = TRUE)
is.ultrametric(phylo_new) # Check if the tree is ultrametric

# Create species vector from community matrix column names
sp <- colnames(comm)
sp <- sp[-1]                # Remove the "site" column
sp <- as.matrix(sp)         # Convert to matrix format

# Replace outdated names (Dennstaedtia -> Mucura)
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Dennstaedtia_globulifera", phylo_new$tip.label)] <- 'Mucura_globulifera'
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Dennstaedtia_bipinnata", phylo_new$tip.label)]   <- 'Mucura_bipinnata'

# Compare species in data with those in the tree
comparison <- name.check(phylo_new, sp, data.names = sp)
length(comparison$data_not_tree) # Number of species not found in the tree

# Extract species absent from the tree
data_not_tree <- comparison$data_not_tree
data_not_tree
length(data_not_tree)
```
### Saving data 

```{r}
# Export the list of unmatched species to Excel for documentation
write.xlsx(
  x = data_not_tree,
  file = "outputs/included_spp.xlsx",
  keepNA = TRUE,
  rowNames = TRUE
)

```

# Finding species on tip labels

```{r}
# Check if specific genera are present in the tree
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Diplazium_h", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Goniopteris_p", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Goniopteris_r", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Parablechnum_c", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Pityrogramma", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Trichomanes_c", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Asplenium_i", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Megalastrum", phylo_new$tip.label)]
phylo_new$tip.label[grepl("Mucura", phylo_new$tip.label)]
```


# Creating 1000 phylo tree 
Here we use Nitta et al (2022) megatree and add species from my community absents in the their tree.

```{r}
# Initialize a list of N copies of the base tree
my.trees <- lapply(1:N, function(x) phylo_new) #insert megatree in a list with 1000 objects
class(my.trees) <- "multiPhylo"   # Set class for multiple phylogenies

# Inspect a few trees
my.trees[[1]]
my.trees[[2]]
is.ultrametric(my.trees[[1]])

# Get list of missing species to add
miss_spp <- comparison$data_not_tree
miss_spp2 <- miss_spp

# Loop to add missing species to each tree
for (j in seq_along(my.trees)) {
  phylotree3 <- phylo_new
  for (i in seq_along(miss_spp2)) {
    nodeages <- branching.times(phylotree3)                  # Get node ages
    phylotree3 <- compute.brtime(phylotree3, method = nodeages) # Compute branch lengths
    phylotree3 <- add.species.to.genus(
      phylotree3,
      miss_spp2[i],
      where = "random"                                       # Randomly place species within genus
    )
  }
  my.trees[[j]] <- phylotree3                               # Save modified tree
}

# Confirm some trees are ultrametric
is.ultrametric(my.trees[[1]])
is.ultrametric(my.trees[[8]])

# Plot example tree
plotTree(my.trees[[1]])

# Inspect Specific Trees (Optional)
my.trees[[1]]
my.trees[[2]]
my.trees[[100]]
```

#1000 phylogenetic trees with just my species

```{r}
# Use keep.tip to keep only the species in `sp`
ntrees <- lapply(my.trees, keep.tip, tip = sp)

# Plot some of the final trees
plot(ntrees[[1]])
plot(ntrees[[2]])
plot(ntrees[[603]])
plot(ntrees[[124]])
plot(ntrees[[435]])
plot(ntrees[[1000]])
```
# Saving trees

```{r}
# Save all 1000 trees as a .txt file in Newick format
mytrees <- ntrees
class(ntrees) <- "multiPhylo"
write.tree(mytrees, "data/new_ftrees.txt")
```
